newsitem.title: COMOROS: Hijacked Ethiopia plane down in sea near Comoros.
newsitem.headline: Hijacked Ethiopia plane down in sea near Comoros.

text.p: A hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 with about 178 passengers and crew aboard crashed into the sea near the Comoro Islands on Saturday and witnesses said there were some survivors.
They said the plane broke in two when it plunged into the sea only metres (yards) from the shore next to a beach hotel about 40 km (25 miles) north of Moroni, the Comoran capital.

The witnesses said 10 bodies were quickly recovered and an unknown number of survivors were taken to hospitals in Moroni and Mitsamiouli. A government official went on state radio to appeal for doctors to go to the hospitals.
A senior official with the airline, Guenet Berhe, told Reuters earlier that the identity and motives of the hijackers were unknown.
The plane was hijacked on Saturday morning soon after it took off from Addis Ababa on a scheduled flight -- number ET 961 -- to Abidjan via Nairobi, Brazzaville and Lagos.
After the hijackers took control, it entered Tanzanian airspace and flew east across the Indian Ocean heading for the Comoro Islands.
A telephone operator at Hotel Le Galawa in the Comoros told Reuters in a telephone call:
"The wreck is about one km (half a mile) off the beach. Part of the fuselage is still afloat. Sixteen injured have been rescued and they are now searching for bodies."
He said the plane had run out of fuel and rough seas were hampering rescue efforts.
Earlier the state airline's general manager, Ahmed Kellow, told Reuters:
"We have very little knowledge of who the hijackers are or their demands."
Ethiopian Airlines is the only airline that crosses the breadth of Africa and has one of the best safety records among African carriers.
